gazetteer_names_needed.name: Kalinjar
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Kalinjar fort, Chandela stronghold in Banda district, Uttar Pradesh, about 80.48 E 25.00 N; left as a name in the Ghurid occupation 1203-1205 and the Mamluk contests of 1233-34 and 1247

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Nadol
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Nadol (Naddula), Pali district, Rajasthan, about 73.23 E 25.20 N; left as a name in the Ghurid 1178 contest with the Chaulukyas and the Kasahrada war zone

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Bathinda
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Bathinda (Tabarhindh), Punjab, India, about 74.95 E 30.21 N; left as a name in the Ghurid 1190-1192 contest with the Chauhans and the Tarain war zone

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Anahilapataka
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Anahilapataka, i.e. Anhilwara/Patan, Chaulukya capital in Gujarat, about 72.12 E 23.85 N; the gazetteer may know it as Patan (Gujarat); left as a name in the Ghurid occupation 1197-1201 and the Aibak Gujarat war zone

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Nuwakot
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Nuwakot, fortress town north-west of the Kathmandu valley, Nepal, about 85.17 E 27.91 N; used in the 1700 gain, the 1744 contest and loss and the Gorkha war zone

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Kirtipur
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Kirtipur, hill town south-west of Kathmandu, Nepal, about 85.28 E 27.67 N; used in the Gorkha conquest war zone

problems: Cliopatria Ceylon (1236-1506) and Kingdom of Dambadeniya (1236-1293) are one Sinhalese realm drawn as two rows with a hole between them; kept as two dossiers, orchestrator may merge or give one colour family.

pandya-empire shares Wikidata Q844910 with pandya-dynasty and ceylon shares Q918153 with british-ceylon: kept as separate states; the colour agent should give pandya-empire the same family and hue as pandya-dynasty.
Cliopatria Gorkha shape from 1762 covers the Kathmandu valley, but Kathmandu fell only in September 1768: the gorkha-kingdom dossier (sa-05) should hold it back to 1768.

Cliopatria Ghurid and Mamluk rows misdivide Muhammad of Ghor's Indian lands 1206-1209 (all Ghurid to 1209, small Mamluk shape from 1210); the dossiers carry the Delhi shape under the Mamluks from 1206 and the other commanders (Yildiz, Qabacha, Tughril, Khaljis) are left without dossiers.
khwarezmid-empire should mirror Ghur vassalage 1206-1215 and the 1215 fall of Ghazni (counterpart ghurid-dynasty).

Cliopatria Mamluk row ends 1293 but the dynasty ended 1290 (the Khalji Revolution, per the Mamluk page); mamluk-dynasty ends 1290 and the khalji-dynasty dossier (another part of this group) should start 1290 rather than Cliopatria's 1294.
